task.name: The runtime half of budget enforcement is sequenced inside run_sprint, so every budget change edits the 3,677-line function even though the decision policy already lives in its own module
task.story_text:
Implementation target: src/theforge/sprint/runner.py

## Problem

`src/theforge/sprint/runner.py` holds 93 top-level definitions across 8,286 lines. One of
them, `run_sprint`, is 3,677 lines — 44% of the module. The next largest is 462.

Budget enforcement is split across that boundary in the worst way. The *decision* half is
already extracted: `sprint/budget.py` owns the pure keep-spending policy (#2547) and
`sprint/unmeasured.py` owns the representation and acceptance of unmeasured spend (#2310),
both testable without a live sprint. But the *runtime* half — the ledger that accumulates
measured spend, carried-spend restoration and disclosure at startup, the pre-dispatch and
in-flight checkpoints that feed the policy its numbers, live budget-status publication, and
budget-triggered cancellation including plan-gate release — is sequenced statements and
nested functions inside `run_sprint` itself.

This concern changes for its own reasons, and has repeatedly: fail-closed on unmeasured
spend (#1992), operator acceptance of bounded unknowns (#2310), carried spend across resume
(#2424), and the in-flight checkpoint (#2547), which alone grew the runner by roughly 500
net lines over five iterations. Each of those changes had to be made inside the same
function body that owns scheduling, dispatch, reconciliation, and teardown, and none of the
runtime behaviour can be tested without constructing the state every other concern expects.

The module is also still growing: ADR-0008 recorded a snapshot baseline of 2,721 and froze
the module at 6,953; it is 8,286 today. #2462 (`sprint/audit_publish.py`) showed the
workable pattern — one concern, moved whole, no back-dependency on the runner.

## Acceptance criteria

- The runtime budget concern — spend ledger, startup carried-spend evaluation and
  disclosure, pre-dispatch and in-flight enforcement moments, live budget-status
  publication, and budget-triggered cancellation — can be changed, read, and tested without
  entering `run_sprint`; `run_sprint` calls it rather than containing it.
- The extracted concern has no import back into the sprint runner, following the pattern
  #2462 established.
- It consumes the decision policy in `sprint/budget.py` and the unmeasured-spend
  representation in `sprint/unmeasured.py` rather than duplicating either; those modules'
  ownership is unchanged.
- The runtime behaviour is directly testable: a test constructs a spend state, exercises an
  enforcement moment, and the concern returns its decision without a sprint running.
- Existing budget-enforcement behaviour remains covered and passes; tests may be relocated
  to exercise the extracted owner directly, without retaining runner-only aliases solely
  for test compatibility.
- Behaviour is unchanged: no sprint outcome, audit field, cost total, cancellation
  classification, or operator-facing string differs as a result.
- Judged on whether this concern became independently changeable, explicitly not on lines
  removed from `runner.py`.

## Example

Where the concern lives today, all inside `run_sprint` (line numbers at `addd2d1c`):

| piece | location |
|---|---|
| `SprintCostLedger` and its observation/snapshot types | runner.py:3398 (module level, but consumed only through `run_sprint`) |
| `_skip_story_for_budget` | runner.py:5724 (nested) |
| `_publish_live_budget_status` | runner.py:5742 (nested) |
| `_budget_decision_for` | runner.py:5761 (nested) |
| `_halt_sprint_for_budget` | runner.py:5793 (nested) |
| `_budget_checkpoint` | runner.py:5829 (nested) |
| `_skip_remaining_stories_for_budget` | runner.py:6826 (nested) |

A budget change today (e.g. #2547's in-flight checkpoint) edits `run_sprint` in several
places separated by thousands of lines of unrelated concerns. After this issue, the same
change would be made in one module with its own tests, and `run_sprint`'s diff would be
limited to the call sites, if it changed at all.

## Notes

This narrows the original filing of this issue, which named the whole of `run_sprint` as
the problem. The full decomposition sequence is recorded in
`docs/plans/2621-runner-decomposition.md`; this issue is deliberately its first slice only,
and later slices are filed one at a time as each becomes current, not as a batch.

Structural-decay observer (#2348, spike) independently ranks this path first by controlled
excess spend: 14 touching runs against its 10-run candidate floor, named in 5 review
findings. The observer's global trust threshold is not met (#2599/#2623), so that ranking
is corroboration; the argument here rests on the measured structure and the change history
above.

handoff.summary: Extracted the runtime half of sprint budget enforcement out of run_sprint into a new sprint-owned module, src/theforge/sprint/budget_runtime.py. The module holds SprintCostLedger/SprintCostSnapshot/SprintCostObservation, checkpoint_cost, copy_worker_signals, and a SprintBudgetRuntime class that owns the operator-acceptance load, carried-occurrence pinning, startup headroom disclosure and refusal, the pre-dispatch and in-flight enforcement moments, live budget-status publication, budget-triggered halt (worker cancellation plus plan-gate release), budget skips, and terminal budget verification. It consumes sprint/budget.py and sprint/unmeasured.py for policy and unmeasured-spend semantics and has no import back into sprint.runner; the two runner-owned side effects a budget refusal causes (_set_outcome, _record_current_story_entry) are injected through bind_story_hooks. The runtime is reached through a new SprintExecutionState.budget field built in __post_init__, so it is not a run_sprint frame local. run_sprint keeps orchestration, scheduling, dispatch, reconciliation and teardown and now calls the owner at each site. run_sprint went 3,816 -> 3,510 lines and runner.py 8,737 -> 8,120, which is a consequence, not the goal.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Two helpers the budget closures call are themselves still nested inside run_sprint — _record_current_story_entry (runner.py:5991, used by _skip_story_for_budget) and _describe_unmeasured_source (runner.py:5574, used by _budget_decision_for). The plan does not say how the extracted module reaches them; naive extraction either drags unrelated concerns along or reintroduces a runner back-import.
  Suggestion: Inject them as callables (or read them off SprintExecutionState) at the module boundary, the way audit_publish.py takes Any-typed state and defers imports; do not import sprint.runner from budget_runtime.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Plan risk 1 (extraction degenerating into parameter threading) is only partly retired. Step 4 adds a back-import guard, but the existing anti-threading guard test_relocated_helpers_take_the_state_not_its_members (tests/test_sprint_runner_structure.py:180) parses runner.py's AST only, so functions in the new module taking individual state members would not be caught.
  Suggestion: Extend the structural guard to also parse the new module's AST for functions whose parameters are SprintExecutionState field names, or accept threading explicitly for the non-state frame locals (accepted_unmeasured, carried_occurrence_ids) that are not state fields.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] The startup carried-spend evaluation/disclosure surface named in the AC is not located in the plan the way the six closures and ledger are; it is currently interleaved with resume/reconcile sequencing in run_sprint.
  Suggestion: Have the dev identify the carried-spend startup block (carried_occurrence_ids / accepted_unmeasured construction and its disclosure logging) explicitly before moving, so this AC is not satisfied only by the checkpoint half.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
